newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel continues to suffer.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel continues to suffer.

text.p: Singapore gas oil market, which is under pressure from a regional glut, continued its downtrend on Friday amid weaker crude values, traders said.
Five sellers again emerged to sell and were forced to lower their offers.
A European major bought from a Singapore trader 150,000 barrels at $22.40 for September 2-6 lifting, free-on-board (fob) basis, 10 cents below the last deal on Monday.
Traders said the seller was due to lift Thai and South Korean gas oil barrels which it had bought recently.
They said the demand outlook remained dim as the market moved to sell solely September barrels next week. A US major was expected to be an active seller next week, they added.
Swaps gas oil also suffered with September trading at $23.25 and later at $23.33 and $23.35. It fell further late in the day and was last indicated at $23.15/$23.25, from Thursday's $23.30/$23.40.

Nepal Oil Corp (NOC) bought by tender 30,000 tonnes of 0.5 percent sulphur diesel for September 21-30 delivery at $176.99 per tonne, cost-and-freight Indian east coast. The seller was a German trader. Nepal bought two cargoes in its last tender for August delivery at $162.69 and $163.44 per tonne, c-and-f.
Jet fuel remained steady at current low levels with a Chinese trader selling a cargo to another European major at $22.80 per barrel for Aug 30-September 3 lifting fob basis.
Three offers were seen on Friday. Traders said the jet fuel market also remained well supplied while buyers have not yet emerged to buy ahead of winter.
